lesson_title: The Honest Banker: Energy Conservation and Power
hook_text: Why is the slide at the park warm by lunchtime? Physics kept the receipt.
clip_script: Every force in the universe is either an honest banker or a toll collector. Gravity? Honest banker. It charges you joules to climb — and repays every single one when you come down, no matter what route you took. Ladder, ramp, staircase: same height, same refund. Friction? Toll collector. It charges per metre of road, keeps the money, and burns it — literally, as heat. That is why the slide at the park is warm by lunchtime: every child who came down paid a toll, and the slide kept the cash. And here's the beautiful part — physics keeps the receipt. A forty-kilogram kid starts two and a half metres up with nine hundred and eighty joules of height-money. She arrives at the bottom with only five hundred joules of speed-money. Where are the missing four hundred and eighty joules? On the receipt: friction's toll, now warming the metal. Nothing in the universe went missing — it just left HER account forever. One equation reads the receipt every time: W n c equals delta E k plus delta E p. Learn to read it, and every slide, ramp and rollercoaster becomes an open book.
visual_style: A split-screen bank: gravity as a tidy teller refunding coins, friction as a gremlin feeding coins into a furnace; then a playground slide with a joule wallet draining from 980 to 500 while a heat shimmer rises off the metal and a paper receipt prints −480 J.
mood: Storybook-sly, warming into a satisfying aha.
pacing: Quick banker-versus-gremlin setup, slow-motion slide with the wallet counting down, receipt-printer snap on the final number.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to read friction's receipt.
